entities.summary: David Beaton was a Scottish cardinal and Archbishop of St Andrews, playing a pivotal role in the Reformation in Scotland. Born around 1480, Beaton rose to prominence as a theological scholar and eventually became the last Scottish cardinal before the Reformation. He played a crucial role in shaping the theological debates of his time, particularly in the area of sacraments. Beaton's leadership and influence led to the establishment of the Church of Scotland, which would eventually become a major force in Scottish history. He died on June 8, 1546, at the age of 65. Beaton's legacy as a reformer and leader has had a lasting impact on Scottish Protestantism and the country's spiritual heritage. The Scottish Reformation, sparked by Beaton's efforts, laid the groundwork for the country's future as a Protestant nation. Beaton's contributions to the theological debates of his time, particularly in the area of sacraments, continue to influence Scottish Presbyterianism to this day. The Reformation, which Beaton helped shape, had far-reaching consequences for Scotland and Europe, shaping the course of European history and the modern Christian Church. The Reformation also had a profound impact on the development of Scottish culture, shaping the country's language, literature, and identity.
